ResourceHeader.Description: GOES-9 Solar X-ray Sensor (SEM/XRS) science-quality Level 2 one-minute average solar X-ray irradiances, provided as daily, annual, and other archived NetCDF files. XRS-A covers 0.05-0.4 nm, and XRS-B covers 0.1-0.8 nm. The product contains one-minute average irradiances, channel quality flags, numbers of samples included in each average, and combined quality flags for samples excluded from averaging. Science-quality irradiances are retrospectively reprocessed using updated calibration and are not reduced by the historical operational scaling factors of 0.85 (XRS-A) and 0.70 (XRS-B). Consult the NOAA GOES 8-15 XRS Science-Quality Data ReadMe for methods and caveats.

NumericalData.ProviderResourceName: NOAA Space Environment Monitor (SEM) Science-Quality Solar X-Ray Sensor (XRS) Data from GOES 1-15
NumericalData.Caveats: GOES-8 through GOES-15 XRS science-quality irradiances may be affected by energetic electron contamination. Unlike GOES-R XRS Science Level 2 1-minute irradiance products, these data have not been corrected for electron contamination.

Parameter.Name: XRS-A primary average flux
Parameter.Description: One-minute average science-quality solar X-ray irradiance in the XRS-A (0.05-0.4 nm) band, derived from GOES-9 XRS observations. The historical operational scaling factor is not applied. Electron contamination is not corrected.
Parameter.Caveats: A systematic calibration discrepancy remains between GOES-8 through GOES-15 XRS-A (short channel) irradiances and GOES-R XRS-A irradiances. The GOES-16/GOES-15 XRS-A ratio is approximately 1.34; this comparison is not a universal per-satellite correction factor. Evidence suggests that GOES-R calibration is more accurate.

Parameter.Name: XRS-B primary average flux
Parameter.Description: One-minute average science-quality solar X-ray irradiance in the XRS-B (0.1-0.8 nm) band, derived from GOES-9 XRS observations. The historical operational scaling factor is not applied. Electron contamination is not corrected.

Parameter.Name: Flags for xrsa_flux
Parameter.Description: One-minute irradiance quality bit mask: 0 good_data, 1 eclipsed_by_earth, 2 saturation, 4 bad_missing_data, and 8 temperature_recovery. Bits may be combined; the temperature_recovery flag is always 0 for GOES-8 through GOES-12. Consult NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.
Parameter.Caveats: Missing measurements are represented by fill values, but the corresponding bad-data quality flags are not always set. Users should check fill values as well as quality flags when screening the data.

Parameter.Name: Flags for xrsb_flux
Parameter.Description: One-minute irradiance quality bit mask: 0 good_data, 1 eclipsed_by_earth, 2 saturation, 4 bad_missing_data, and 8 temperature_recovery. Bits may be combined; the temperature_recovery flag is always 0 for GOES-8 through GOES-12. Consult NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.
Parameter.Caveats: Missing measurements are represented by fill values, but the corresponding bad-data quality flags are not always set. Users should check fill values as well as quality flags when screening the data.

Parameter.Name: Number of averaged measurements in xrsa_flux
Parameter.Description: Number of valid higher-cadence samples contributing to the corresponding one-minute average irradiance.

Parameter.Name: Number of averaged measurements in xrsb_flux
Parameter.Description: Number of valid higher-cadence samples contributing to the corresponding one-minute average irradiance.

Parameter.Name: Flags on data excluded from xrsa_flux average
Parameter.Description: Bitwise union of condition flags on higher-cadence measurements excluded from the corresponding one-minute irradiance average. See NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: Flags on data excluded from xrsb_flux average
Parameter.Description: Bitwise union of condition flags on higher-cadence measurements excluded from the corresponding one-minute irradiance average. See NetCDF flag_masks and flag_meanings.

Parameter.Name: Record start time
Parameter.Description: Start time of each one-minute average, in seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, neglecting leap seconds.
